name: Pistol, two hands

contact.why: the firing palm wraps the grip's right side and its backstrap, the web of the hand high under the tang on the backstrap's middle, so the thumb lies along the left side (FM 3-23.35 2-3); the fingers forward across the front strap, square to the grip's 18.7 degree slant
contact.fit_source: FM 3-23.35 (2003) figures 2-1 and 2-2: the palm on the grip's firing side, the middle finger's first segment across the front strap just under the trigger guard, the trigger finger along the frame above the guard; placed on this gun's own faces (panel x -1.67, front strap y -1.3 to -2.1, frame side x 1.75 at the guard)

index.source: Ninapro calibrated kinematics (Jarque-Bou, Atzori, Mueller 2020, CC BY 4.0), exercise 3, median of 10 subjects' steady holds; angles outside the joint's range dropped, a dropped ring angle the mean of middle and little, a dropped end joint two thirds of the middle joint; movement 4, index finger extension grasp
index.why: the trigger finger straight along the frame, off the trigger until the shot (FM 3-23.35 2-1)

middle.source: Ninapro calibrated kinematics (Jarque-Bou, Atzori, Mueller 2020, CC BY 4.0), exercise 3, median of 10 subjects' steady holds; angles outside the joint's range dropped, a dropped ring angle the mean of middle and little, a dropped end joint two thirds of the middle joint; movement 4
middle.why: the middle finger wrapped round the front strap, pressing to the rear (FM 3-23.35 2-1)

ring.source: Ninapro calibrated kinematics (Jarque-Bou, Atzori, Mueller 2020, CC BY 4.0), exercise 3, median of 10 subjects' steady holds; angles outside the joint's range dropped, a dropped ring angle the mean of middle and little, a dropped end joint two thirds of the middle joint; movement 4
ring.why: the ring finger wrapped round the front strap, pressing to the rear (FM 3-23.35 2-1)

pinky.source: Ninapro calibrated kinematics (Jarque-Bou, Atzori, Mueller 2020, CC BY 4.0), exercise 3, median of 10 subjects' steady holds; angles outside the joint's range dropped, a dropped ring angle the mean of middle and little, a dropped end joint two thirds of the middle joint; movement 4
pinky.why: the little finger wrapped round the front strap, pressing to the rear (FM 3-23.35 2-1)

thumb.source: Ninapro calibrated kinematics (Jarque-Bou, Atzori, Mueller 2020, CC BY 4.0), exercise 3, median of 10 subjects' steady holds; angles outside the joint's range dropped, a dropped ring angle the mean of middle and little, a dropped end joint two thirds of the middle joint; movement 4
thumb.why: the firing thumb rests alongside the weapon without pressure, along the frame's support side above the trigger guard (FM 3-23.35 2-1, figure 2-1)

trigger.why: the trigger finger's pad on the trigger for the shot

contact_rules.why: the firing thumb lies forward along the frame's support side, over the safety, its pad on the frame (FM 3-23.35 (2003) 2-3: the two-hand grip)
the web of the hand high on the backstrap, under the tang (FM 3-23.35 (2003) 2-3: the two-hand grip)
the trigger finger straight along the frame's firing side above the trigger guard, off the trigger until the shot (FM 3-23.35 2-1): it sets the hand's height, and with it the thumb's
the palm on the grip's firing side and backstrap (FM 3-23.35 (2003) 2-3: the two-hand grip)
the middle finger round the front strap just under the trigger guard (FM 3-23.35 (2003) 2-3: the two-hand grip)
the ring finger round the front strap under the middle finger (FM 3-23.35 (2003) 2-3: the two-hand grip)
the middle fingertip reaches round onto the grip's support side (a smaller hand on a wide grip may stop on the front strap)

contact.why: the support palm on the grip's left side, filling what the firing hand leaves open (FM 3-23.35 2-3)
contact.fit_source: FM 3-23.35 (2003) 2-2, the fist grip: the support fingers over the firing fingers, the support palm's heel on the bare support-side panel; on this gun's faces (panel x 1.67, the palm's fitted half thickness 1.84 cm and the glove)

index.source: Ninapro calibrated kinematics (Jarque-Bou, Atzori, Mueller 2020, CC BY 4.0), exercise 3, median of 10 subjects' steady holds; angles outside the joint's range dropped, a dropped ring angle the mean of middle and little, a dropped end joint two thirds of the middle joint; movement 5, medium wrap
index.why: the support index finger between the firing middle finger and the trigger guard (FM 3-23.35 2-2)

middle.source: Ninapro calibrated kinematics (Jarque-Bou, Atzori, Mueller 2020, CC BY 4.0), exercise 3, median of 10 subjects' steady holds; angles outside the joint's range dropped, a dropped ring angle the mean of middle and little, a dropped end joint two thirds of the middle joint; movement 5
middle.why: the support fingers closed over the firing fingers (FM 3-23.35 2-2)

ring.source: Ninapro calibrated kinematics (Jarque-Bou, Atzori, Mueller 2020, CC BY 4.0), exercise 3, median of 10 subjects' steady holds; angles outside the joint's range dropped, a dropped ring angle the mean of middle and little, a dropped end joint two thirds of the middle joint; movement 5
ring.why: the support fingers closed over the firing fingers (FM 3-23.35 2-2)

pinky.source: Ninapro calibrated kinematics (Jarque-Bou, Atzori, Mueller 2020, CC BY 4.0), exercise 3, median of 10 subjects' steady holds; angles outside the joint's range dropped, a dropped ring angle the mean of middle and little, a dropped end joint two thirds of the middle joint; movement 5
pinky.why: the support fingers closed over the firing fingers (FM 3-23.35 2-2)

thumb.source: Ninapro calibrated kinematics (Jarque-Bou, Atzori, Mueller 2020, CC BY 4.0), exercise 3, median of 10 subjects' steady holds; angles outside the joint's range dropped, a dropped ring angle the mean of middle and little, a dropped end joint two thirds of the middle joint; movement 5
thumb.why: the support thumb alongside the firing thumb, forward along the frame (FM 3-23.35 2-2)

slide_rear.why: the slingshot (the action's rack): the support hand grips the slide's rear serrations from the gun's left and top, the fingers over the top to the right side, the thumb on the left side; the forearm stays near its middle roll

index.why: the fingers close on the slide's right serrations

middle.why: the fingers close on the slide's right serrations

ring.why: the fingers close on the slide's right serrations

pinky.why: the fingers close on the slide's right serrations

thumb.why: the thumb's ball against the slide's left side

slide_front.why: the press check: the hand over the slide's front, fingers and thumb pinching its sides to ease it back

index.why: the index and middle pinch the slide's right side

thumb.why: the thumb on the slide's left side

mag_grab.why: the magazine's base in the palm from below and the gun's left (the support hand's side, so the forearm turns no further than it can), the fingers along its front, the thumb along its back; the heel of the hand seats it

index.why: the fingers along the magazine's front

middle.why: the fingers along the magazine's front

ring.why: the fingers along the magazine's front

pinky.why: the fingers along the magazine's front

thumb.why: the thumb along the magazine's back

contact_rules.why: the support thumb forward along the frame's support side under the firing thumb, clear of the slide (FM 3-23.35 (2003) 2-3: the two-hand grip)

the support palm's heel fills the grip's support-side panel the firing hand leaves bare: no space left on the grip, the gun held in a closed ring of both hands against recoil (FM 3-23.35 2-2, the fist grip)

stance.why: both arms out in front with the elbows a little bent, the pistol below the line of sight and a little right of it (a two-handed ready hold; aimed, it rises to the eye); a guess at the first-person view

rules: both thumbs below the slide's lower edge (clear of the slide's path)
the trigger finger off the trigger outside the trigger clips

sources.title: FM 3-23.35, Combat Training with Pistols M9 and M11 (2003)
FM 23-35, Basic Field Manual: Automatic Pistol, Caliber .45 (1940)
